title: Standardize IaC storage module for EBS/EFS/S3 with lifecycle, snapshots, and encryption defaults
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a single Terraform module (registry-style) that teams can consume for provisioning EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, and S3 buckets in Private/VPC deployments. The module must: 1) enforce encryption-by-default (KMS-managed keys with optional customer keys), 2) create snapshot/backup lifecycle policies with sensible defaults and optional retention overrides, 3) provide cross-account snapshot sharing and IAM roles for restore workflows, 4) expose healthcheck hooks (CloudWatch metrics + Lambda remediation) and 5) maintain backwards-compatible inputs to make upgrades from existing hand-rolled modules straightforward.
acceptance_criteria: Module accepted in internal Terraform registry and consumed by at least two internal repos (private-deploy and onprem-connector)
Default encryption enabled: EBS volumes use aws_kms_key alias redwood/ebs or customer-supplied key; EFS and S3 enforce server-side encryption with KMS
Snapshot lifecycle: daily automated snapshots for EBS, weekly EFS backups (via backup service or scripts), and S3 lifecycle rules that transition to IA/GLACIER after configurable days
Healthchecks: CloudWatch alarm template emitted by module for >3 failed snapshot attempts in 24h and an optional Lambda remediation that retries once and pages if still failing
Upgrade path documented with a migration guide and automated tfstate import helpers to avoid data loss
Module passes security review and a Chaos test (simulate API throttling) without data loss during snapshot operations
decisions: Use a composable module with three submodules (ebs, efs, s3) rather than a monolith to make teams opt-in to only what they need
Default KMS keys are created by the module for convenience, but production customers must provide a key_arn to opt into their own CMKs
We will implement snapshot scheduling using AWS Backup for EBS + EFS where available; fallback to Lambda-based snapshots in regions without Backup support
Cross-account snapshot sharing will be opt-in via a boolean flag and requires a list of trusted AWS account IDs to be provided
We will keep Terraform 1.5-compatible constructs and avoid v0.12-era hacks to ease upgrades
tradeoffs: Creating KMS keys by default improves developer onboarding but increases audit scope and principal management; opted to make it optional for enterprise customers
Using AWS Backup centralizes policies but adds cost and regional availability constraints; module supports both Backup and a lighter-weight Lambda snapshotter

Tighter defaults (short retention) reduce storage costs but increase risk of accidental data loss; we choose conservative retention defaults (30d EBS, 90d EFS, 365d S3 transition) and expose overrides
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): deploy module with default settings into dev accounts and validate snapshot creation and restore flows
Stage 2 (staging): enable KMS customer key option and run upgrade migration guide against existing tfstate; monitor costs for 2 weeks
Stage 3 (prod canary): onboard one business unit and validate cross-account share and healthchecks
Stage 4 (general): publish to internal registry and announce with migration docs and a Slack office hours session
migration_steps: Identify current hand-rolled storage resources via terraform state list and cloud inventory
Run provided import helper script (scripts/import-ebs.sh) to map existing EBS volumes into the new module stateful resource names
For S3, create a temporary ACL-preserving import plan or use bucket replication to migrate lifecycle rules before switching producer stacks
Run terraform plan in dry-run mode and review proposed resource replacements; use terraform state mv where possible to avoid recreate
Execute in canary account with operator supervision, validate snapshot restores, then proceed to other accounts
test_plan: Unit tests: Terratest suite for module inputs/outputs and plan-only asserts
Integration: create ephemeral dev environment, create EBS/EFS/S3 resources, run snapshot + restore, validate data integrity
Security tests: KMS key permissions audit, ensure no public S3 buckets created by default
Chaos: simulate AWS Backup API throttling and verify Lambda fallback retries and alarm triggers
monitoring_healthchecks: Emit CloudWatch metric namespace Redwood/StorageModule with dimensions {Account,Region,ResourceType}
Alarm: SnapshotFailures > 3 in 24h => SNS topic redwood-ops with runbook link
Optional Lambda: retry snapshot action once, tag failure, and escalate to PagerDuty if still failing
Expose a module output (healthcheck_endpoint) to wire into Console observability dashboards
